Breakfast. At 09:00, set out on a sightseeing tour of Lima that includes a visit to the Casa Aliaga house museum.

Begin in Miraflores, one of Lima's most scenic and modern neighbourhoods. Visit Parque del Amor, see the ancient Huaca Pucllana archaeological complex from a viewpoint, stroll through the well-known Olive Grove Park and see colonial mansions that recall an earlier era.

Continue to the historic centre, home to Lima's main architectural and cultural landmarks. See the Plaza Mayor, the cathedral, the Church and Convent of San Francisco, the Presidential Palace, City Hall and other landmarks in the old city.

A highlight is Casa Aliaga, a historic mansion considered one of the oldest inhabited houses in the Americas. Its history dates to 1536, when Spanish conquistadors were founding Lima. The house was built for Jerónimo de Aliaga, an associate of Francisco Pizarro, on the site of a pre-Columbian structure.

The mansion has remained in the same family for nearly five centuries, passing from one generation to the next. Its interiors, antique furniture, artworks and surviving period details offer a glimpse into Peru's past and into the lives of the Spanish aristocracy in the colonial era.

After the tour, transfer to the airport and fly to Cusco, the ancient capital of the Inca Empire.

On arrival, you'll be met at the airport and taken to the 4-star Xima Cusco hotel or a hotel of the same category.
